statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk 20% sits at the lower edge of the watch band, five points below the block threshold.
recommendation: Mapped policy state WATCH applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Tail remains below the block threshold because the recovery into the Friday cash open is a retracement that held Thursday's support shelf, with no aligned cross-asset amplifier. The published danger window spans 13:30Z to 15:30Z, covering the cash open and the 14:00Z Michigan preliminary release; opening-auction continuation and post-release structure were unobserved at the assessment cutoff.
headline: Nasdaq-100 recovery gap carries into the Friday cash open; Tail at the lower edge of the watch band ahead of Michigan
body: NQ December futures trade at 31,216.25 (+246.75, +0.80%) against a 30,969.50 prior close, with an overnight range of 30,953.00-31,266.50, and the QQQ premarket print one minute before the bell was 752.63 (+0.68%). Both readings date from the 13:17Z-13:30Z window, so the gap into the 13:30Z cash open is verified but post-open structure is not: this assessment deliberately does not claim opening-auction continuation. The move retraces Thursday's 1.39% Nasdaq-100 decline to 30,725.81, the worst session in roughly seven weeks, which followed a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualised revenue was about $50bn at end-September, roughly $20bn below figures previously circulated to investors; the gap is largely an accounting difference over whether cloud-partner revenue is counted. Cross-assets are not aligned for a pathological path. VIX is 15.17 (-1.56%) in a 15.10-15.34 range with no volatility expansion, WTI November crude is 90.77 (-0.79%) after Thursday's roughly 4% surge with Brent near $102, and the 10-year Treasury is 5.26% (+3bp) against H.15 readings of 5.28% and a 2-year of 4.77% on 7 October. Oil retreating and VIX easing remove rather than add amplifiers, while the rate channel is the one that tightened. The near-term checkpoint is the 14:00Z Michigan preliminary October release, consensus 48.0 against 48.1 prior with 1-year inflation expectations 4.6% prior and 5-10 year 3.4% prior; a median year-ahead figure of 3.9% for September is already in the news flow as the highest since May 2023, and minutes indicate most officials see a likely need for a further 25bp hike by year end. Event importance of that kind raises Stress and informs Confidence rather than Tail until an observed price path establishes mean-reversion failure. Stress stays elevated at 58% on the combination of the unresolved AI-revenue narrative, a semiconductor gauge down 3.4% on Thursday, yields near two-decade highs, oil above $90 and the continuing Iran conflict with Strait of Hormuz disruption. Confidence is 87%: current levels, yields, oil, volatility, the catalyst stack and the verified seven-day calendar are all in hand, with the single gap being post-open intraday structure. Shared Finviz context was read and found stale at 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with collectionStatus partial, so it was excluded and independent research carried the assessment.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span Thursday's AI-led decline and the overnight recovery into Friday's cash open. Tail peaked at 28% (orange, trend-down) in the 17:00Z slot as the OpenAI revenue report drove the Nasdaq-100 down 1.39% and the semiconductor gauge down 3.4%, with Stress reaching 72%. Risk then decayed steadily across the US close and the Asian and European sessions as futures retraced higher: Tail returned to the 16-18% low band from 20:00Z onward and Stress fell from the mid-60s to 46% by 10:00Z, with the dominant mode shifting to trend-up from 07:00Z as the recovery extended. The last two slots turned Stress back up to 49% and 54% and the mode back to mixed as the cash open and the Michigan release approached. All 24 slots are available from published Claude history and are reproduced as they were assessed at the time.
outlookSummary: The window splits into eight live hours and sixteen closed ones. Tail rises from 20% to a 23% peak in the 14:00Z slot, covering the just-completed 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z Michigan preliminary release, then decays through the US afternoon to 18% before a second, smaller 21% cluster at 20:00Z for the cash close and the scheduled Collins remarks. Every live-hour value stays in the watch band or below: the published structure is a retracement that held support with no aligned cross-asset amplifier, and the contract requires observed persistent one-way extension or multiple independent current amplifiers before Tail blocks. CME equity index futures halt at 21:00Z on Friday, so the remaining sixteen slots describe a closed venue in which no mean-reversion failure can occur; Tail falls to an 11-13% floor and Confidence steps down from 87% to 75% to record the absence of live price discovery rather than any benign structural read. Latent weekend gap risk from the Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption would express only at the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, which lies outside this window.
